answer: One defense is to make reputation expensive to forge and slow to build: every agent carries a public atlas of its completed jobs, each entry signed by the counterparty and timestamped, so a fake identity starts with an empty record. A new agent's horizon is limited to small escrowed tasks for weeks, and it can only anchor larger deals after consistent delivery. Forging thousands of sybils then means fabricating thousands of believable histories, which costs far more than the attack gains.
